payload.description: Give E-1785's contract a lever at the system-prompt layer by authoring a bespoke Claude Code output style, and ship it to users as an embedded Go template rather than a hand-written file. Every mechanism E-1785 shipped sits in user-turn context (CLAUDE.md), an event-triggered nudge (E-1803), or a post-hoc gate (E-1901, parked); an output style occupies a fourth position none reach — injected into the system prompt and re-asserted every turn — which is the durability CLAUDE.md lacks. This does NOT replace or reverse E-1911: it improves only the ORGANIC half of E-1911's contract, while `task report` keeps producing the appended computed block that carries the guarantee. Scope is "b" per user direction: response shape plus the discharged-fact test and veracity rule that obsolete E-1876 never delivered. Because a style is a file on disk, new users must get one without hand-authoring it, via an embedded Go template wired into `project init` and/or the `setup` group.
payload.text:
# Spec

## 1. Style content (scope "b")

Start at "b" and optimize from there, per user direction. The style carries:

1. **Response shape** — no preamble or postamble; do not re-narrate what a tool just
   printed; do not summarize a file the user is about to read.
2. **The discharged-fact test** — what agent output may leave unsaid.
3. **The veracity requirement** — any surfaced fact must be verified against live
   state at the moment of surfacing, never recalled.

(2) and (3) are the parts of E-1876 that went obsolete undelivered: E-1911 replaced
E-1876 without shipping them. A style is a better host for them than a hook, because
they describe how to write, not a condition to detect.

Consider folding in E-1893 (replies restate the task IDs they are about) — it is
style-shaped and currently unplanned.

Author **one** style, not several: only one can be active at a time, and multiple
bespoke styles fragment the contract.

Set `keep-coding-instructions: true` in frontmatter (see analysis — the trap).

## 2. Delivery via embedded Go template

An output style is a file on disk, so new users must not have to hand-author it. Put
the initial value in the Go executable so it ships with install, following the
`internal/templatecmd` / E-1565 pattern: `//go:embed`, lookup order of per-developer
local override -> committed project copy -> embedded fallback, materialized on first
use so users can customize it.

**Open decision to make and document:** does the style install to the user-global
Claude output-styles directory (applies to every session on the machine) or the
project-scoped one (endless only)? Project-scoped is the safer default — a tool
should not silently reshape unrelated sessions — but the user's goal is broader than
one project, so this needs an explicit call rather than a silent default.

## 3. Wiring

Endless has two plausible homes, both currently Python:

- `endless project init` (aliased `register`) — registers the DB row, scaffolds `.endless/`
- the `endless setup` group — `claude-hook`, `prompt-hook`, `shell-helpers`,
  `channel-plugin`, each with a `remove-` counterpart

Decide: a new `endless setup output-style` + `remove-output-style` pair, a step inside
`project init`, or both. Match the group's existing conventions — including the
`remove-` counterpart, which every other member has.

**Go/Python split:** `setup` and `project init` live in Python (`src/.../setup.py`,
`register.py`) while the embed must be Go. Reconcile with E-1486 (remove all Python
SQLite access by porting to Go) rather than working around it — do not add a new
Python-calls-Go shim if E-1486's direction makes the command Go-native anyway.

## 4. Acceptance

- Style file authored and materializable from embed.
- Install and remove paths both work and match `setup` group conventions.
- Installing the style does **not** drop the default `anti_verbosity`,
  `action_caution`, or `task_continuity` sections — verify empirically, do not assume
  the `keep-coding-instructions` default.
- No doc, guide section, or help string references the removed `/output-style`
  command.
- E-1911's appended curated block still renders unchanged alongside the style.
- Degrades legibly when the `outputStyles` safe-mode gate disables custom styles.
payload.analysis:
# Mechanism findings — verified against the installed Claude Code build (2.1.220)

These were read out of the shipped executable's strings, not recalled. An earlier
answer in the filing session asserted `/output-style` existed and was wrong; treat
harness priors as stale until confirmed against the installed build.

## The command is gone; it is a /config row now

There are zero slash-command registrations named `output-style`. It survives as:

- a `/config` panel row: `id:"outputStyle", label:"Output style", type:"managedEnum",
  options:Object.keys(_fe), optionsHint:"For custom styles, open /config."`
- a `/config key=value` key: `output-style` -> `Output style`
  (`/config` declares `supportsNonInteractive:!0`, `argumentHint:"key=value"`)

No doc, guide text, or help string this task produces may tell users to run
`/output-style`.

## Why this position beats the ones E-1785 already used

Style content is injected into the system prompt, and separately re-asserted every
turn as a meta system-reminder:

    output_style:(e)=>{let t=_fe[e.style];if(!t)return[];
      return pm([zr({content:`${t.name} output style is active. ${e.turnReminder??
        "Remember to follow the specific guidelines for this style."}`,isMeta:!0})])}

CLAUDE.md is injected once into user-turn context and competes with everything else
in a long session. The Stop hook (E-1901) fires after the tokens already exist and
produces a bounce loop, which is why E-1911 parked it. The per-turn re-assertion is
the property neither has.

## No built-in style helps — the "just switch styles" step would backfire

From the `_fe` built-in map:

- `default` -> `null`. Injects nothing at all.
- `Explanatory` -> literally "you may exceed typical length constraints".
- `Learning` -> pauses to ask the user to hand-write 2-10 line code pieces.
- `Proactive` -> autonomy (execute immediately, minimize interruptions), not length.

`default` is already the only built-in that adds no prose. Authoring is the only path.

## Frontmatter surface for custom styles

Confirmed key aliases: `keep-coding-instructions` -> `keepCodingInstructions`, and
`force-for-plugin` -> `forceForPlugin` (plugin-only; warns "has force-for-plugin set,
but this option only applies to plugin output styles. Ignoring." elsewhere). Plus
`name` and `description`.

`turnReminder` is built-in-only — it is not in the frontmatter alias list, and only
`Proactive` sets one. A custom style therefore gets the generic fallback reminder
text. Still per-turn, just not custom-worded.

## TRAP: a careless style can delete the anti-verbosity instructions

All three built-ins set `keepCodingInstructions:!0`. The default system prompt is
assembled from named sections via `sD(...)`, and one is literally called
`anti_verbosity`:

    m=[sD(`anti_verbosity${s}${f?":send_user_msg":""}`,()=>oMy(t)),
       sD("pronouns",()=>cMy),
       sD(`action_caution${s}`,()=>iMy(t)),
       sD("task_continuity",()=>sMy(...

A style that omits `keep-coding-instructions: true` risks dropping the very
anti-verbosity instructions the task is trying to strengthen. Set it explicitly and
verify empirically — do not assume the flag's default.

## Safe-mode gate

`fd("outputStyles")` gates custom styles: when set, the loader returns only the
built-in map and the config row renders the value as "<name> (disabled in safe mode)".
Any install path must degrade legibly under that gate rather than appearing to work.

## Existing precedent to follow for delivery

`internal/templatecmd` (E-1565) already does exactly the embed-and-materialize shape
this task needs: `//go:embed all:templates`, and a per-template lookup order of
`.endless/templates/<name>.local.tmpl` (per-developer) -> `.endless/templates/<name>.tmpl`
(committed, materialized from embed on first render) -> embedded fallback. Reuse the
pattern rather than inventing a second one.
